title: Design and application of CAM‐xanthate hydrogel for high‐capacity adsorption of copper and nickel ions
content:
Abstract

Water contamination by toxic heavy metals is a major environmental challenge, necessitating the development of efficient and sustainable adsorbents. In this study, a cellulose-based CAM-Xanthate hydrogel was synthesized and applied for the removal of Cu2+ and Ni2+ ions from aqueous solutions. Three hydrogel grades were prepared and evaluated for their swelling behavior, with CAM-Xanthate-2 showing the highest swelling capacity of 306.78 g/g in distilled water, 263.62 g/g in tap water, and 237.21 g/g in gray water after 670 min. The hydrogels were comprehensively characterized using UV–Visible spectroscopy, FT-IR, TGA, SEM, and point of zero charge (pHpzc) analysis. CAM-Xanthate-2 demonstrated excellent adsorption performance, achieving removal efficiencies of 96.36% for Cu2+ and 94.44% for Ni2+ ions. Adsorption equilibrium data followed the Langmuir isotherm model, with maximum adsorption capacities of 324.59 mg/g for Cu2+ and 317.14 mg/g for Ni2+ ions. Kinetic studies indicated that adsorption followed the pseudo-second-order model, with rate constants of 7.88 × 10−4 and 7.78 × 10−4 g/(mg·min) for Cu2+ and Ni2+ ions, respectively, suggesting a chemisorption-controlled process. The hydrogel also exhibited good reusability, maintaining desorption efficiencies of 82.67% (Cu2+) and 80.25% (Ni2+) after 5 cycles. Overall, CAM-Xanthate-2 hydrogel showed strong potential as an effective, reusable, and sustainable adsorbent for the removal of heavy metals from contaminated water, with promising applicability in industrial wastewater treatment.
